title: The Merry crowd at the fair
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）　|　核心词汇：merry　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 merry 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the porter wrote of ① a merry crowd at the fair in the journal, and everybody in the coast said at once that it was ② merrier than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the porter, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the merry ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the merriest crowd at the fair anybody in the coast had ever seen, or so the journal for August 1987 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too merry to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the merry ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bag at the far cove, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a merry song in the kitchen, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as merry as the song in the kitchen they had once had in the old coast. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was merry or not, and he said so.

By 2000 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something merry, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next coast called the whole plan ⑧ quite merry; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the merry ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2003, in silence, she wrote of another merry crowd at the fair in the same journal, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ merrier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The merriest song in the kitchen in the whole coast, she said in 2005, was the one she could never quite name; the merry ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 欢乐（前置定语 a merry crowd at the fair：1993 年挑夫在行记里记下的那件欢乐的人群）
B. adj. 欢乐／愉快（比较级 merrier than：文中两处，一处比集市上欢乐的人群，一处比预想）
C. adj. 欢乐／愉快（最高级 the merriest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 欢乐（表语 too merry to do：母亲觉得它太欢乐，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 愉快（前置定语 a merry song in the kitchen：叔叔把整件事称作一桩愉快的歌）
F. adj. 愉快（同级比较 as merry as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厨房里欢快的歌相比）
G. adj. 愉快（后置定语 something merry：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 愉快（受程度副词修饰 quite merry：那位游客的评价）

items.q: a merry crowd at the fair
the merriest crowd at the fair anybody
a merry song in the kitchen
The merriest song in the kitchen in

answers.why: merry 意为“欢乐”，1993 年挑夫在行记里记下的是“一件欢乐的人群”，此处作前置定语 a merry crowd at the fair。
merry 意为“欢乐”，此处用比较级 merrier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
merry 意为“欢乐”，行记上 八月 那行字说它是海岸里最欢乐的一件，故用最高级 the merriest crowd at the fair。
merry 意为“欢乐”，母亲认为这件东西“太欢乐了，谁也用不上”，too merry to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
merry 意为“愉快”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩愉快的歌”，此处作前置定语 a merry song in the kitchen。
merry 意为“愉快”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厨房里欢快的歌一样愉快”，同级比较用 as merry as。
merry 意为“愉快”，行记上那半行字要的是“愉快的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something merry。
merry 意为“愉快”，邻海岸来的那位游客认为这套计划“相当愉快”，quite 修饰原级 merry。
merry 意为“愉快”，2003 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要愉快”，故用比较级 merrier than。
merry 意为“愉快”，母亲 2005 年说的是“整个海岸里最愉快的那一桩”，故用最高级 the merriest song in the kitchen。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1993 年，挑夫在行记里记下了一件欢乐的人群。（a merry crowd at the fair）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更欢乐。（merrier than …）
母亲觉得它太欢乐，谁也用不上。（too merry to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩愉快的歌。（a merry song in the kitchen）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厨房里欢快的歌一样愉快。（as merry as …）
到了 2000 年，行记上只剩半行字：要的是一件愉快的东西。（something merry）
answers: In 1993 the porter wrote of a merry crowd at the fair in the journal.
Everybody said it was merrier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too merry to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a merry song in the kitchen.
He said nobody would call it as merry as the song in the kitchen they had once had.
By 2000 the journal asked for nothing but something merry.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 merry 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the porter wrote of a merry crowd at the fair in the journal, and nobody forgot it.
It was the merriest crowd at the fair in the coast, or so the journal says.
My mother thought it too merry to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a merry song in the kitchen, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next coast called the plan quite merry, and everybody laughed.
The merry ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
